verdicts.note: Assessor since 2015, appraiser in the office from 2007 [S1][S2], re-elected 2022 [S4], WACO executive board and 11 years chairing the assessors' technology committee [S1][S2]. He runs on that record. No evidence points the other way.

Both sources are his own words: the pamphlet line against 'unnecessary tax increases' [S1] and his campaign release on 'fighting bills that would increase property taxes' through the assessors' legislative committee [S2]. The office does not set taxes [S3], so -1 at medium is the right ceiling. The second source is advocacy on property-tax bills, which keeps this above a lone platitude.

Renewal direction holds against an 11-year incumbent: no elected experience [S1], and he says core duties 'have been neglected' and he can 'lead towards restoring public trust' [S2]. The basis paraphrases this as arguing the office 'needs new leadership'; S2 implies that but does not say it. Four years as a staff appraiser in the same office [S1][S3] keeps it at +1, medium.
